subs.1: GateReady. Know before the gate review.
subs.2: Automotive suppliers develop parts through phase gates. Before each gate review, a quality engineer checks by hand that every piece of evidence is in place.
subs.3: Is the PFMEA approved? Does the Control Plan reflect the last design change? Is any high-risk item still open?
subs.4: The evidence already lives in Confluence and Jira. Checking it takes hours, and what gets missed shows up in the review or in a customer audit.
subs.5: GateReady is a Forge app inside the Jira project. One click checks every gate against live Jira and Confluence data.
subs.6: Brake Sensor Housing is 88 percent ready for the Process Design gate.
subs.7: GateReady checks validity, not just existence. The PFMEA is approved and has every required section, but Recommended Actions only says "TBD". So it asks a person to look.
subs.8: EV Battery Bracket uses the same template and sits at the same gate. It is 38 percent ready.
subs.9: The PFMEA is still in progress. The Control Plan is approved, but older than the last design change. The MSA plan is missing, and two high-risk items are open.
subs.10: Every verdict comes with the finding and a link to the evidence.
subs.11: Each gap becomes a Jira work item, assigned to the owner of that evidence, with the finding and links attached.
subs.12: Run it again and nothing is duplicated.
subs.13: The owner updates the Control Plan. Check again.
subs.14: Readiness moves from 38 to 50 percent, and GateReady shows exactly which requirement changed.
subs.15: Every check is kept in the gate's history: when, by whom, and how ready it was. That is the audit trail.
subs.16: Gates, rules, owners and the linked Confluence space are configured per project.
subs.17: Six rule types cover documents and work items: exists, approved, up to date, required sections, all done, and none open.
subs.18: Start from the APQP template, copy another project's plan, or build your own.
subs.19: The Gate Review Agent runs the same deterministic check in conversation and explains each finding.
subs.20: Rules cannot judge whether content is good enough, so the agent reads the document and gives an opinion, clearly marked as advisory. It never changes a verdict.
subs.21: Before it writes anything, it shows what it will create and asks.
subs.22: The review summary is waiting as a Confluence draft: readiness, open gaps, the evidence checklist, and a place for the decision.
subs.23: After the review, record the gate as passed. GateReady saves the date and the readiness at that moment, and moves the project to its next gate.
subs.24: The same six actions are exposed as an MCP server and packaged as a reusable skill, so other agents can prepare gate reviews too.
subs.25: GateReady runs entirely on Atlassian. No data leaves the platform.
subs.26: GateReady. For quality engineers and project managers who need to know before the gate review, not during it.
